_comment: CBCT Dental Report Template v3 - rewritten against schema_v3.json (mandible/maxilla/dental_arch/dental_elements arrays, no category/role fields). Path convention: 'mandible.X', 'maxilla.X', 'dental_arch.X' reference a fact by its fact_id directly (matching schema_v3's flat top-level arrays); 'dental_elements.tooth_{fdi}_X.field' references a per-tooth fact, substituting the real FDI for {fdi}. KEY RULE (new in v3): every fact below that has a free-text 'findings'/'details' field uses it AS THE PRIMARY OUTPUT whenever it's non-empty -- v3's schema leans on free text far more than v2.0 did, so the template must surface it rather than only deriving sentences from the structured enum/bool fields. Structured fields still drive WHICH branch fires (is this abnormal at all?) and are the fallback wording when findings is empty.

metadata.structure: Preamble (dentition type + whole-mouth periodontal condition), then two arch paragraphs (Mandible, Maxilla) with no sub-headers, then a whole-mouth impacted-teeth note (not reliably splittable by arch since affected_teeth is free-text location, not strict FDI), then a closing significant-negative-findings line. Order within each arch: scope, condyles+canals (mandible only) / sinuses+nasal cavity (maxilla only), alveolar bone atrophy, bone quality, dental arch findings, tooth detailed findings, prosthetic findings.

helpers_used_pervasively.findings_or_fallback: THE core v3 pattern. Given a fact with both structured fields and a findings/details string: if findings is_meaningful, output it verbatim as the sentence (it's written to already be a complete clinical sentence). If findings is empty but the structured fields indicate an abnormality, fall back to a templated sentence built from those fields. If findings is empty AND fields are all normal, output nothing.
helpers_used_pervasively.is_meaningful: not null, not empty string/list/dict, not in normal_enum_values for strings (unchanged from v2.0)

components._canal_note: schema v6.4 replaced the canal's course enum (regular|lingual|buccal) with location (lingual|buccal). location is a position, true of every canal, so it can no longer license an abnormal-course sentence and there is no 'regular' value left to gate on: each side always gets the regular-course sentence, and location surfaces only inside the adjacent-teeth clause, where it relates to the roots the canal passes. Implemented in synthesize_report.render_canal.

rules.output: Right mandibular canal with a regular course{adjacent_clause}.
Left mandibular canal with a regular course{adjacent_clause}.

rules.fallback: Mandible with {extent}-degree atrophy of the edentulous ridge.

shared_components._comment: Referenced by $ref from both mandible_findings and maxilla_findings above -- identical logic, each instantiated with that section's own fdi_range for filtering dental_arch's whole-mouth list-type facts.

absent_teeth.note: filter to this arch's fdi_range before classifying

rules.condition: nearly edentulous (all but 1-3 teeth per quadrant), one quadrant
rules.output: Complete edentulism of the {quadrant_roman} quadrant except for {remaining_teeth_list}.

rules.condition: full quadrant edentulous, one quadrant only

wisdom_teeth.note: only the two wisdom-tooth facts belonging to this arch apply (mandible: lower_left/lower_right = 38/48; maxilla: upper_right/upper_left = 18/28). Absent wisdom tooth -> handled by absent_teeth above (eruption_state=='absent' also covers this, so don't double-report). upper_right/upper_left carry a 'findings' field the lower two don't -- use it when present.

rules.condition: otherwise, eruption_state != 'fully_erupted' OR orientation != 'normal' OR impacted != 'none'
rules.note: one sentence per tooth, ascending FDI order, all applicable conditions combined per tooth per the two lines above

collection_empty_fallback.output_maxilla: Teeth from 18 to 28 are present in the arch.

For the 4 wisdom teeth this is a deliberate independent cross-check against dental_arch's dedicated wisdom-tooth facts (same value expected from both, not merged) -- if they disagree, that's a signal to flag for review, not silently pick one.

rules.condition: eruption_state != 'fully_erupted' AND tooth is NOT a wisdom tooth

rules.output: Fixed prosthetic bridge from {span_start} to {span_end}, with {anchors_clause} and {pontics_clause}. {details}
Fixed prosthetic bridge from {span_start} to {span_end}, with {anchors_clause} and {pontics_clause}.

bridge.anchors_clause: "anchor abutment teeth on {abutment_teeth_joined}" and/or "an implant in the {implant_supported_teeth[0]} region" / "implants in the {implant_supported_teeth_joined} regions" (from implant_supported_teeth)
bridge.pontics_clause: "pontic in the {pontic_teeth[0]} region" / "pontics in the {pontic_teeth_joined} regions" (from pontic_teeth)

empty_prediction.definition: all facts are empty AND all dental_elements facts.detected in ['no', 'no_image', null]

normal_case.definition: prediction has real data but no abnormalities

helpers.is_meaningful: not null, not empty string/list/dict, not in normal_enum_values for strings
helpers.merge_findings: join per-tooth findings with semicolons; if multiple, wrap in period
helpers.affected_teeth: convert list of FDI numbers to comma-separated string with 'and' before last
helpers.filter_by_fdi_range: given a list of FDI numbers (or a list of objects with an FDI-bearing field) and an [lo, hi] range, keep only entries whose FDI falls in that arch's range -- used everywhere a dental_arch (whole-mouth) fact needs to contribute to only one arch's paragraph
helpers.classify_absent_teeth_pattern: given the absent-teeth FDI list filtered to one arch (spanning 1-2 quadrants), classify into: (a) few missing/non-edentulous -- consecutive run vs non-consecutive scatter; (b) nearly edentulous -- all but 1-3 teeth missing in a quadrant, one quadrant or both; (c) full quadrant edentulous -- entire quadrant missing, one or both. Drives the absent_teeth rule table in shared_components.dental_arch_findings.
helpers.group_by_quality: group a list of {fdi, quality} pairs into one sentence per distinct quality value, e.g. all 'inadequate' teeth in one clause, all 'overfilled' in another -- used for the endodontic_treatment filling-quality followups
helpers.phrase_position_list: render a list of FDI positions as 'position 15' (single) or 'positions 26 and 27' (multiple), matching implants.location's expected phrasing
helpers.findings_or_fallback: see helpers_used_pervasively above -- the core v3-specific pattern: prefer a fact's own findings/details free text verbatim over any templated sentence built from its structured fields
